analysis.title: The anatomy of a market panic (Life after the great liquidation)
key_insights: SPX is at its most oversold levels since Liberation Day and the COVID crash, and is testing the trendline in place since the late-2022 lows.
VXN took out Liberation Day panic levels and closed at its highest since April 2020. The gap between NDX and inverse VXN is described as beyond extreme.
Semis vol hit records: VXSMH made fresh all-time highs (index dates only to 2022) after Friday's SOX selloff. The note suggests this may be the time to buy semis panic.

GS PB data show hedge funds cutting risk aggressively. US single-stock shorting was the highest weekly level since June 2022 and third highest in a decade, and ETF shorts rose 11% in one week. Data run through Thursday and miss Friday's selling.
Fundamental L/S net leverage fell to 42.3%, 1st percentile over the past year. Beta-adjusted net leverage dropped more than 22 points since early October to 48.2%, a five-year low.

GS says hedge fund global positioning is near 10-year lows, HFs sold tech at the fastest pace on record over six weeks, and CTA NDX futures positioning is near the bottom of its 10-year range. GS thinks the unwind is closer to the end than the beginning, though CFTC non-dealer positioning remains near highs.
GS's Peter Callahan says NDX trades at 17x forward earnings and semis at 12-13x. Charts price in earnings cuts while fundamentals are solid and estimates still rise, but buyers are missing.
Tech drawdown relative to SPX is the second largest in 20+ years.
GS Vol Panic Index ended last week at 9.8/10, historically a signal to add risk. But in prior episodes above 9 with the Fed hiking, SPX returned just +0.4% on average over the next three months.
Short gamma could magnify moves in both directions, and the NDX 2018 analogy suggests a furious bounce followed by another leg lower.

tension_points.bull_case: Panic index at 9.8/10, hedge fund positioning near decade lows, NDX at 17x and semis at 12-13x forward earnings, estimates still rising, so conditions for a violent bounce are in place.
tension_points.bear_case: The Fed is hiking, and prior panic episodes above 9 under hikes returned just +0.4% over three months. The 2018 NDX analogy implies a bounce then another leg lower, with short gamma amplifying moves.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A bounce that fades into another leg lower, as in the 2018 analogy.
